You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

Workspace: JacobianChallenge
Project: Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
Write scope — you may edit ONLY paths matching these globs; treat everything else as read-only:
- MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/**
- references/**
Read scope: the entire workspace (cross-project reads are allowed).
Log/artifact directory: .archon-horizon/runs/0027/sessions/0014-horizon-rebuild

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

$$\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C/k}\ \text{representable},\qquad \dim_{k}\mathrm{Pic}^{0}_{C/k}=g,\qquad \forall\,(C,P)\to A\ \exists!\ \mathrm{Pic}^{0}\to A.$$

# Memory
- Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target" is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension recipe.

- **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension; blow-up needed). Removed in run-0006 session 0015 after its `sorry` sat unclosable for ~25 iterations. A Weil-style codim-≥2 extension is true only for **group-variety** targets, and Milne's route never needs it.
- **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`): Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative); Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry) must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).
- **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`, reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom` where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`); rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (= `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`, positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).
- **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).
- **FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**

State after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements — Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):

- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.
- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` — no defeq walls anywhere in this file).
- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) — `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Caveat 1 — pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient ⟨sorry⟩` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.
- Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.
- **Σ-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app` at `⊤` (+ `homOfLE le_top = 𝟙 ⊤` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' ≫ fromTildeΓ).app ⊤ ∘ toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.
- **Recipes: module-level dévissage in Lean v4.31 (landed in FlatteningStratification GenericFreeness, run 0010 T12 r2) — reuse for any prime-filtration/SES argument.**

- **ModuleCat SES arguments need ONE universe**: `ModuleCat.ofHom {X Y : Type v}` forces all modules of a `ShortComplex (ModuleCat R)` into the same universe. Binders `{M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*}` give distinct universes and produce baffling failures — instance goals displayed as raw `Quot ⇑(OreLocalization.oreEqv ...)` (LocalizedModule unfolded past its instance heads) plus universe-mismatched `Eq.{max u_1 u_4}` vs `Eq.{max u_1 u_2}`. 11	# Universal sections: `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, 𝒪) = A` for every `k`-algebra `A`
12	
13	Brick 2 of the separatedness ledger (design §4.4): for the proper, geometrically integral
14	curve `C` over the field `k` and **every** commutative `k`-algebra `A`, the second
15	projection induces an isomorphism `A ≅ Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤)`. This is the form of
16	Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` ("`𝒪_S ≅ f_*𝒪_X` holds universally", *The Picard Scheme* §3.11)
17	actually consumed downstream: by the étale-separatedness argument (C1), by the
18	dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and by the χ-ledger over field extensions
19	(`A = K`).
20	
21	## Main declarations
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isIso_appTop_snd_overSpec` — the keystone: the pullback of global
24	  sections along the second projection, `Γ(Spec A, ⊤) ⟶ Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, ⊤)`,
25	  is an isomorphism.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.universalSections` — the bundled form
27	  `CommRingCat.of A ≅ Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, ⊤)`; its `hom` is by definition the
28	  `A`-algebra structure map of the global sections of the base change induced by the
29	  second projection (the `A`-algebra face of the statement).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.universalSectionsEquiv` — the same as a ring equivalence
31	  `A ≃+* Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, ⊤)`.
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.universalSections_self` — the **consistency gate** (design §7.2,
33	  lane L3): at `A := k` the isomorphism is Wave 1's `Γ(C.left, 𝒪) ≅ k`
34	  (`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_hom_appTop_of_geometricallyReduced`, `Curve/Sections.lean`)
35	  transported along the first projection — which is an isomorphism because
36	  `Spec k ⟶ Spec k` is.

40	`⊤ ⊆ C.left` is quasi-compact (properness) and quasi-separated (separatedness), so the
41	qcqs master square `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections` (brick 1, via mathlib's

### 4.4 Why one plus suffices: the separatedness ledger

**(C1) Separatedness** (`Picard/Separatedness.lean`): for affine `T` and a presented étale
cover `E`, the map `relPic C T → relPic C (T' E)` is injective. This is Kleiman 2.5(1)
restricted to what we consume, recast on cocycles. Proof ledger (all pieces named because they
are shared bricks):

1. `sectionsBaseChange` (`Cohomology/SectionsBaseChange.lean`): for `V ⊆ C.left` affine open
   and a `k`-algebra `A`, `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, V_A) ≅ Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A`, naturally.
   *Shared with*: the T₀ dual-numbers engine (`A = k[ε]`, recon lesson 7) and the χ-ledger over
   field extensions (`A = K`). One brick, three consumers.
2. `universalSections` (`Picard/UniversalSections.lean`): `Γ((C ⊗ Spec A).left, ⊤) = A` for
   every `k`-algebra `A` — the two-cover H⁰ slice: the complex
   `Γ(V₀) ⊕ Γ(V₁) → Γ(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` has `H⁰ = k` (Wave 1), stays exact under the flat `⊗[k] A`
   by 1. This is our discharge of Kleiman's `ex:gc&r` hypothesis in the form actually consumed.
3. `prPullback_injective`: `CechPic.map (snd C T).left` is injective for affine `T` — a unit
   cocycle on `C ⊗ T` trivializing must have come from `T`, because
   `𝒪ˣ((C ⊗ V).left) = Γ(V)ˣ` by 2 (applied on an affine pointed cover of `T`). Hence the
   H_T-quotient loses nothing it shouldn't, and "which `N`" in a `pr^*N`-equation is unique.
4. `Descent/InvertibleModule.lean` (pure algebra, PR-candidate): along a faithfully flat ring
   map `A → B`, an invertible `B`-module with a descent datum descends to an invertible
   `A`-module, uniquely up to canonical isomorphism. (Survey: this exists **nowhere** in
   mathlib — "no effective descent of modules"; it is the honest algebraic core of both (C1)
   and (C2).)
5. Assembly (Kleiman's 2.5(1) argument recast): a class `λ ∈ relPic C T` dying on the cover
   gives, via 3 applied over `T'` and `T' ×_T T'`, a line-bundle class `n'` on `T'` with a
   descent datum along `Spec B → Spec A`; by 4 it descends to `n` on `T`, and `λ = pr^* n`
   follows from 3 again. Hence `λ = 0` in the quotient.

**Choice discipline (binding).** Constructions like 4's descended module and §2.6(b)'s
uniformizers may use `Classical.choice` *internally*, provided the resulting `CechPic`/`relPic`
**class** is proven independent of the choices (the allowed axiom set is `propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound`). What remains forbidden (route rule 3/4) is storing mere
existence (`Nonempty`) where downstream needs data — in particular the `JacobianData` fields.

**(C2) Comparison under a section** (`Picard/Rigidification.lean`; statement Wave 3, proof may
slip to Wave 4 — OPEN-2): if `C ⊗ T → T` has a section `σ` (equivalently `T ⟶ C ⊗ T` over
`T`), then `picEtAffUnit : relPic C T → PicEtAff C T` is bijective. This is Kleiman 2.5(2)
recast; ledger: `lm:idn` (rigidified pairs = relPic, cocycle form: normalize a cocycle so that
`σ`-pullback is 1), `lm:aut` (no automorphisms: a unit on `C ⊗ T` restricting to 1 along σ is
1, by `universalSections`), then effectivity of the rigidified descent datum by Zariski-locally
reducing to brick 4 on an affine pointed cover of `C ⊗ T` (the datum's cocycle coherence comes

11	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:

13	covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
14	stabilized along the refinement preorder.

17

25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
26	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.

45	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
46	  iseqv := by

49	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩

167	lemma mk_one (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : mk 𝒰 (1 : X.unitsH1 𝒰) = 1 :=
168	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒰, le_rfl, le_top, by rw [map_one, map_one]⟩
169	
170	@[simp]
171	lemma mk_mul_mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a b : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
172	    mk 𝒰 a * mk 𝒰 b = mk 𝒰 (a * b) := by
173	  rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
174	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒰, le_rfl, inf_le_left, ?_⟩
175	  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_rfl]
176	
177	@[simp]
178	lemma mk_inv (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : (mk 𝒰 a)⁻¹ = mk 𝒰 a⁻¹ :=
179	  rfl
180	
181	/-! ## Functoriality: pullback of Picard classes -/
182	
183	private def mapSig (f : X ⟶ Y) (p : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
184	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
185	  ⟨p.1.pullback f, f.pullbackUnitsH1 p.1 p.2⟩
186	
187	private lemma mapSig_compat (f : X ⟶ Y) :
188	    ∀ {p q : Σ 𝒰 : Y.PointedCover, Y.unitsH1 𝒰}, p ≈ q → mapSig f p ≈ mapSig f q := by
189	  rintro ⟨𝒰, a⟩ ⟨𝒱, b⟩ ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
190	  refine ⟨𝒲.pullback f, PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁,
191	    PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂, ?_⟩
192	  show unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₁) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
193	      = unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h₂) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
194	  rw [Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₁ a, Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 f h₂ b, e]
195	
196	/-- Contravariant functoriality of the Čech Picard group: pull the cover back pointwise,
197	pull the unit cocycles back through `f`, restrict. -/
198	def map (f : X ⟶ Y) : Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic where
199	  toFun := Quotient.map (mapSig f) fun _ _ h ↦ mapSig_compat f h
200	  map_one' := by
201	    show mk ((⊤ : Y.PointedCover).pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 ⊤ 1) = 1
202	    rw [map_one, mk_one]
203	  map_mul' a b := by
204	    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
205	    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
206	    show mk ((𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f)
207	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱) (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b))
208	      = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) *
209	          mk (𝒱.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒱 b)
210	    rw [mk_mul_mk_inf]
211	    refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).pullback f, le_rfl,
212	      le_inf (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_left)
213	        (PointedCover.pullback_mono f inf_le_right), ?_⟩
214	    simp only [map_mul, ← Hom.unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
215	
216	@[simp]
217	lemma map_mk (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (a : Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
218	    map f (mk 𝒰 a) = mk (𝒰.pullback f) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) :=
219	  rfl
220	
221	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along the identity is the identity. -/
222	@[simp]
223	theorem map_id (X : Scheme.{u}) : map (𝟙 X) = MonoidHom.id X.CechPic := by
224	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
225	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
226	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X)) ((𝟙 X : X ⟶ X).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a) = mk 𝒰 a
227	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X) ≤ 𝒰 := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
228	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (𝟙 X), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
229	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
230	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
231	  ext x y T a b
232	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
233	    γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf]
234	  exact id_unitsAppLE _ _
235	
236	/-- Pullback of Picard classes along a composite (the lane keystone). -/
237	theorem map_comp (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) : map (f ≫ g) = (map f).comp (map g) := by
238	  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x ↦ ?_
239	  induction x using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
240	  show mk (𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g)) ((f ≫ g).pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
241	    = mk ((𝒰.pullback g).pullback f)
242	        (f.pullbackUnitsH1 (𝒰.pullback g) (g.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a))
243	  have hle : 𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g) ≤ (𝒰.pullback g).pullback f := fun x ↦ le_of_eq (by simp)
244	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰.pullback (f ≫ g), le_rfl, hle, ?_⟩
245	  induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ =>
246	  refine congrArg (Quot.mk _) ?_
247	  ext x y T a b
248	  rw [OneCocycle.res_ev, OneCocycle.res_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev,
249	    Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev, Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE]
250	  rfl
251	
252	/-! ## Sanity gate: triviality over a field -/
253	
254	/-- On a scheme with a subsingleton underlying space — e.g. `Spec` of a field — the
255	Čech Picard group is trivial: every pointed cover is a cover by a single open, on which
256	every unit cocycle is a coboundary. -/
257	instance subsingleton_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] :
258	    Subsingleton X.CechPic := by
259	  refine ⟨fun p q ↦ ?_⟩
260	  induction p using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
261	  induction q using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
262	  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱, inf_le_left, inf_le_right, ?_⟩
263	  have := H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat)
264	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens (fun i j ↦ le_of_eq (congrArg _ (Subsingleton.elim i j)))
265	  exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
266	
267	/-- The Čech Picard group of the spectrum of a field is trivial. -/
268	theorem eq_one_of_subsingleton (X : Scheme.{u}) [Subsingleton X] (x : X.CechPic) :
269	    x = 1 :=
270	  Subsingleton.elim x 1
271	
272	example {K : Type u} [Field K] (x : (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).CechPic) : x = 1 :=
273	  eq_one_of_subsingleton _ x
274	
275	end CechPic
276	
277	end Scheme
278	
279	end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# Base change of sections along the projection `C ⊗ Spec A ⟶ C`
10	
11	For an object `C` of `Over (Spec k)` (`k` a field), a commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and a
12	quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ C.left`, this file identifies the sections of the
13	base change `(C ⊗ Spec A).left` over the preimage `V_A := (fst C (Spec A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V` of
14	`V` under the first projection with the tensor product of the sections over `V`:
15	
16	`Γ(C.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left, V_A)`
17	
18	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`), sending `s ⊗ a` to the product of the two
19	pullbacks (`sectionsBaseChange_tmul`), compatibly with restriction along `W ≤ V`
20	(`sectionsBaseChange_naturality`). Here `C ⊗ T` is the cartesian-monoidal product of
21	`Over (Spec k)`, realized by `Limits.pullback`; the single bridge lemma between the two
22	languages is `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`.
23	
24	This is brick 1 of the separatedness ledger (design §4.4): one brick, three consumers —
25	étale separatedness (arbitrary `A`), the dual-numbers tangent engine (`A = k[ε]`), and the
26	χ-ledger under field extension (`A = K`). Hence the statements are for an arbitrary
27	commutative `k`-algebra `A`, and `V` is allowed to be any quasi-compact quasi-separated
28	open (e.g. the intersection of two affines of the curve), not just an affine one.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left` — the bridge: for `X T : Over S`, the scheme-level
33	  square `(fst X T).left, (snd X T).left, X.hom, T.hom` is a pullback.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.overSpec k A` — `Spec A` as an object of `Over (Spec k)`, together with
35	  the instance `Flat (overSpec k A).hom` (automatic over a field).
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` by
37	  restriction of scalars along the structure morphism. Deliberately **not** a global instance
38	  (house rule, cf. `Scheme.overModule`); consumers activate it with
39	  `attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.resAlgHom` — restriction of sections as a `k`-algebra homomorphism.
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections_of_isAffineOpen`,
42	  `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_sections` — the master pushout squares on sections, for
43	  an arbitrary test object `T` with `T.left` affine (affine `V` needs no flatness; qcqs `V`
44	  needs `[Flat T.hom]`).
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections` — the same square with the
46	  `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)`/`Γ(Spec A, ⊤)` corners replaced by `k` and `A`.
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.sectionsBaseChange`
48	  — the comparison isomorphism (in `CommRingCat`, resp. as a ring equivalence), with the
49	  computation rules `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one`, `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`,
50	  `sectionsBaseChange_tmul` and the restriction-naturality
51	  `sectionsBaseChange_naturality`.
52	
53	## Implementation notes
54	
55	The heavy lifting is mathlib's `pushoutSection` API
56	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Flat.lean`): for a pullback square of schemes the
57	canonical map `Γ(X, Uₓ) ⊗[Γ(S, Uₛ)] Γ(T, Uₜ) ⟶ Γ(X ×ₛ T, ...)` is an isomorphism for
58	affine `Uₛ, Uₜ` and qcqs `Uₓ` when `T ⟶ S` is flat — which over a field is automatic.
59	This file only supplies the Over-category bridge, the corner bookkeeping (`ΓSpecIso`), and
60	the tensor-product face.
61	
62	The `k`-linear faces consumers may need are one line away from `sectionsBaseChange`:
63	it is `k`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one` applied to
64	`algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V) r` (both sides land in the structure-map image), and
65	`A`-algebra-compatible by `sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul`.
66	-/

145	  have hUSX : V ≤ X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=

149	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, inf_top_eq]

155	`T.left` affine, and a quasi-compact quasi-separated open `V ⊆ X.left` (e.g. an
156	intersection of two affine opens of a separated scheme, or all of a proper curve), the

160	Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(X.left, V)

164	```

166	is a pushout of commutative rings. Flatness of `T.hom` holds automatically for

168	theorem Over.isPushout_sections [Flat T.hom] (hT : IsAffineOpen (⊤ : T.left.Opens))
169	    {V : X.left.Opens} (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left))
170	    (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
171	    IsPushout (X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge))
172	      (T.hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge)
173	      ((fst X T).left.appLE V ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
174	      ((snd X T).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
175	        (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X T).left).ge)) := by
176	  have hUST : (⊤ : T.left.Opens) ≤ T.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
177	    (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top T.hom).ge
178	  have hUSX : V ≤ X.hom ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (Spec (.of k)).Opens) :=
179	    le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge
180	  have hUY : (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V =
181	      (fst X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ V ⊓ (snd X T).left ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : T.left.Opens) := by
182	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top, inf_top_eq]
183	  have h := isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right
184	    (Over.isPullback_left X T) hUST hUSX hUY (isAffineOpen_top _) hT hV hV'
185	  exact (isIso_pushoutSection_iff _ _ _ _).mp h
186	
187	end Pushout

189	section TensorFace

191	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (X : Over (Spec (.of k)))
192	
193	/-- The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` for `X` an object of `Over (Spec k)`:
194	restriction of scalars along the structure morphism `X.hom`. Deliberately **not** a global
195	instance (it would overlap with mathlib's `Algebra R Γ(Spec R, U)` instances; cf. the house
196	rule for `Scheme.overModule`). Activate it locally with
197	`attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra` — the statements of this file mention it
198	explicitly, so consumers must activate the same instance for the statements to elaborate
199	identically. -/
200	@[reducible] noncomputable def Over.sectionsAlgebra (V : X.left.Opens) :
201	    Algebra k Γ(X.left, V) :=
202	  ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫
203	    X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge)).hom.toAlgebra
204	
205	attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra
206	
207	/-- Unfolding lemma for `Over.sectionsAlgebra`: the algebra structure map, as a morphism of
208	`CommRingCat`, is the structure morphism of `X` on sections. -/
209	lemma Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections (V : X.left.Opens) :
210	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)) =
211	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫
212	        X.hom.appLE ⊤ V (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top X.hom).ge) :=
213	  rfl
214	
215	/-- The algebra structure maps of `Over.sectionsAlgebra` intertwine restriction. -/
216	lemma Over.algebraMap_sections_comp_res {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
217	    CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)) ≫ X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op =
218	      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, W)) := by
219	  rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Category.assoc,
220	    Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
221	
222	/-- Restriction of sections along `W ≤ V` as a `k`-algebra homomorphism (with the
223	`Over.sectionsAlgebra` structures). -/
224	noncomputable def Over.resAlgHom {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
225	    Γ(X.left, V) →ₐ[k] Γ(X.left, W) where
226	  __ := (X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
227	  commutes' r := congr($(Over.algebraMap_sections_comp_res X h).hom r)
228	
229	@[simp]
230	lemma Over.resAlgHom_apply {V W : X.left.Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(X.left, V)) :
231	    Over.resAlgHom X h s = X.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op s :=
232	  rfl
233	
234	variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
235	
236	/-- **Base change of sections with the `k`/`A` corners.** For a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`, the
237	square
238	
239	```
240	   k    ⟶ Γ(X.left, V)
241	   |         |
242	   ↓         ↓
243	   A    ⟶ Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)
244	```
245	
246	(with the `Over.sectionsAlgebra` structure map on top and the second-projection pullback
247	`A ≅ Γ(Spec A, ⊤) ⟶ Γ(..)` at the bottom) is a pushout of commutative rings. -/
248	theorem Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections {V : X.left.Opens}
249	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
250	    IsPushout (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Γ(X.left, V)))
251	      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
252	      ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl)
253	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
254	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
255	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) := by
256	  refine (Over.isPushout_sections X (overSpec k A)
257	    (isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A) hV hV').of_iso
258	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)) (Iso.refl _) (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)) (Iso.refl _)
259	    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
260	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
261	    rw [Over.ofHom_algebraMap_sections, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
262	  · have h : (overSpec k A).hom.appLE ⊤ ⊤ (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (overSpec k A).hom).ge =
263	        (overSpec k A).hom.appTop :=
264	      Scheme.Hom.appLE_eq_app _
265	    rw [h, overSpec_hom]
266	    exact Scheme.ΓSpecIso_naturality (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
267	  · simp only [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id, Category.id_comp]
268	  · rw [Iso.refl_hom, Category.comp_id]
269	    exact (Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc _ _).symm
270	
271	/-- **Base change of sections, comparison isomorphism** (in `CommRingCat`):
272	`Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≅ Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)` for a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`.
273	On pure tensors this is the product of the two pullbacks; see
274	`Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul`. -/
275	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso {V : X.left.Opens}
276	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
277	    CommRingCat.of (Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) ≅
278	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
279	  (CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).isoIsPushout _ _
280	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')
281	
282	/-- **Base change of sections** (brick 1 of the separatedness ledger, design §4.4): for `X`
283	over the field `k`, a commutative `k`-algebra `A` and a qcqs open `V ⊆ X.left`, the ring
284	equivalence `Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+* Γ((X ⊗ Spec A).left, fst⁻¹ V)`, sending `s ⊗ a` to
285	the product of the pullbacks of `s` (along the first projection) and of `a` (along the
286	second). The `k`-algebra structure on `Γ(X.left, V)` is `Over.sectionsAlgebra`. -/
287	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChange {V : X.left.Opens}
288	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) :
289	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
290	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
291	  (Over.sectionsBaseChangeIso X A hV hV').commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
292	
293	/-- `Over.sectionsBaseChange` for an affine open `V` (affine opens are qcqs) — the form
294	pinned by design §4.4 brick 1. -/
295	noncomputable def Over.sectionsBaseChangeOfIsAffineOpen {V : X.left.Opens}
296	    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
297	    Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A ≃+*
298	      Γ((X ⊗ overSpec k A).left, (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) :=
299	  Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV.isCompact hV.isQuasiSeparated
300	
301	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one {V : X.left.Opens}
302	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
303	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) :
304	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ 1) =
305	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s :=
306	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inl_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
307	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom s)
308	
309	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
310	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left)) (a : A) :
311	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (1 ⊗ₜ a) =
312	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
313	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
314	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a :=
315	  congr($((CommRingCat.isPushout_tensorProduct k Γ(X.left, V) A).inr_isoIsPushout_hom _ _
316	    (Over.isPushout_algebraMap_sections X A hV hV')).hom a)
317	
318	/-- The base-change equivalence on a pure tensor: `s ⊗ a` goes to the product of the
319	pullback of `s` along the first projection and the pullback of `a` along the second. -/
320	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul {V : X.left.Opens}
321	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
322	    (s : Γ(X.left, V)) (a : A) :
323	    Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' (s ⊗ₜ a) =
324	      (fst X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE V ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V) le_rfl s *
325	      ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv ≫
326	        (snd X (overSpec k A)).left.appLE ⊤ ((fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
327	          (le_top.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_top (snd X (overSpec k A)).left).ge)) a := by
328	  have h : (s ⊗ₜ[k] a : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) = (s ⊗ₜ 1) * (1 ⊗ₜ a) := by
329	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul, mul_one, one_mul]
330	  rw [h, map_mul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul_one, Over.sectionsBaseChange_one_tmul]
331	
332	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
333	/-- **Naturality of the base-change equivalence in the open**: for `W ≤ V` (both qcqs),
334	restricting the base-changed section is base-changing the restriction. The map on tensor
335	products is `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` of the restriction `Over.resAlgHom` and the
336	identity of `A`. -/
337	theorem Over.sectionsBaseChange_naturality {V W : X.left.Opens}
338	    (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X.left)) (hV' : IsQuasiSeparated (V : Set X.left))
339	    (hW : IsCompact (W : Set X.left)) (hW' : IsQuasiSeparated (W : Set X.left))
340	    (hWV : W ≤ V) (x : Γ(X.left, V) ⊗[k] A) :
341	    (X ⊗ overSpec k A).left.presheaf.map
342	        (homOfLE (show (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W ≤
343	          (fst X (overSpec k A)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V by gcongr)).op
344	      (Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hV hV' x) =
345	      Over.sectionsBaseChange X A hW hW'
346	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (Over.resAlgHom X hWV) (AlgHom.id k A) x) := by
347	  induction x with
348	  | zero => simp only [map_zero]
349	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
350	  | tmul s a =>
351	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq, Over.resAlgHom_apply,
352	      Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, Over.sectionsBaseChange_tmul, map_mul]
353	    congr 1
354	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply,
355	        Scheme.Hom.map_appLE]
356	    · rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Category.assoc, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
357	
358	end TensorFace

9	/-!
10	# Unit-valued Čech cocycles on pointed covers and their pullback
11	
12	This file sets up the cocycle-level substrate of the Čech Picard group
13	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic`):
14	
15	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PointedCover`: one open per point, containing it; a
16	  `SemilatticeInf` with an `OrderTop`, refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`,
17	  and pullback along a morphism of schemes.
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsCocycle`, `Scheme.unitsH1`: unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles
19	  and `H¹` on a pointed cover; `Scheme.unitsRes`: restriction along a refinement, a group
20	  homomorphism, strictly functorial (`unitsRes_unitsRes`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsEvInf`, `Scheme.unitsRestrict`: the pair values of a
22	  unit cocycle and restriction of unit sections, retyped through `Γ(X, U)ˣ`. Statements
23	  phrased through these are honestly `Γ`-typed, so `rw`/`simp` work on them; goals arising
24	  from the `OneCochain` field types (whose carriers go through `unitsPresheaf.obj`) are
25	  closed against them by `exact` — the two spellings are definitionally equal.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle`, `Hom.pullbackUnitsH1`: pullback of
27	  unit cocycles and their `H¹` classes along a morphism of schemes, compatible with
28	  restriction (`unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1`) — the substrate for `CechPic.map`.
29	
30	The file starts with generic `evInf` algebra for `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups`
31	(values of cochains/cocycles at binary infima commute with `1`, `*`, `⁻¹`); it lives here
32	only because `CechH1.lean` is at the file-size cap, and should move alongside
33	`OneCochain.evInf` when that file is split for a mathlib PR.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe w' w u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
41	
42	namespace CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
43	
44	-- Generic `evInf` algebra; lives here only because `CechH1.lean` is at the file-size cap.
45	-- Move alongside `OneCochain.evInf` when that file is split for the mathlib PR.
46	
47	variable {P : Type u} [SemilatticeInf P] {I : Type w'} {G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}} {U : I → P}
48	
49	@[simp]
50	lemma OneCochain.one_evInf (i j : I) : (1 : OneCochain G U).evInf i j = 1 :=
51	  rfl
52	
53	@[simp]
54	lemma OneCochain.mul_evInf (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) :
55	    (γ₁ * γ₂).evInf i j = γ₁.evInf i j * γ₂.evInf i j :=
56	  rfl
57	
58	@[simp]
59	lemma OneCochain.inv_evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) :
60	    (γ⁻¹).evInf i j = (γ.evInf i j)⁻¹ :=
61	  rfl
62	
63	@[simp]
64	lemma OneCocycle.one_evInf (i j : I) : (1 : OneCocycle G U).evInf i j = 1 :=
65	  rfl
66	
67	variable {Gc : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{w}}
68	
69	@[simp]
70	lemma OneCocycle.mul_evInf {U : I → P}
71	    (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (Gc ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) (i j : I) :
72	    (γ₁ * γ₂).evInf i j = γ₁.evInf i j * γ₂.evInf i j :=
73	  rfl
74	
75	@[simp]
76	lemma OneCocycle.inv_evInf {U : I → P}
77	    (γ : OneCocycle (Gc ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) (i j : I) :
78	    (γ⁻¹).evInf i j = (γ.evInf i j)⁻¹ :=
79	  rfl

82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
83	
84	namespace Scheme
85	
86	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
87	
88	/-! ## Pointed covers -/
89	
90	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. Pointed covers
91	are the index discipline of `Scheme.CechPic`: the index type is the carrier of `X` (so
92	everything stays in `Type u`), refinement is indexwise, and pointwise `⊓` makes the
93	refinement order directed. -/
94	structure PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
95	  /-- The member of the cover attached to a point. -/
96	  opens : X → X.Opens
97	  /-- Each point lies in its member. -/
98	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
99	
100	namespace PointedCover
101	
102	@[ext]
103	lemma ext {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : ∀ x, 𝒰.opens x = 𝒱.opens x) : 𝒰 = 𝒱 := by
104	  cases 𝒰; cases 𝒱
105	  simpa using funext h
106	
107	instance : SemilatticeInf X.PointedCover where
108	  le 𝒱 𝒰 := ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x
109	  le_refl 𝒰 x := le_rfl
110	  le_trans 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := (h₁ x).trans (h₂ x)
111	  le_antisymm 𝒰 𝒱 h₁ h₂ := ext fun x ↦ le_antisymm (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
112	  inf 𝒰 𝒱 :=
113	    { opens := fun x ↦ 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x
114	      mem_opens := fun x ↦ ⟨𝒰.mem_opens x, 𝒱.mem_opens x⟩ }
115	  inf_le_left 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_left
116	  inf_le_right 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_right
117	  le_inf 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := le_inf (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
118	
119	instance : OrderTop X.PointedCover where
120	  top := { opens := fun _ ↦ ⊤, mem_opens := fun _ ↦ trivial }
121	  le_top _ _ := le_top
122	
123	lemma le_def {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x :=
124	  Iff.rfl
125	
126	@[simp]
127	lemma inf_opens (𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (x : X) :
128	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x = 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x :=
129	  rfl
130	
131	@[simp]
132	lemma top_opens (x : X) : (⊤ : X.PointedCover).opens x = ⊤ :=
133	  rfl
134	
135	/-- The pullback of a pointed cover along a morphism of schemes: the pointed cover by
136	preimages, `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`. -/
137	def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) : X.PointedCover where
138	  opens x := f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x)
139	  mem_opens x := 𝒰.mem_opens (f.base x)
140	
141	@[simp]
142	lemma pullback_opens (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (x : X) :
143	    (𝒰.pullback f).opens x = f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x) :=
144	  rfl
145	
146	lemma pullback_mono (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 𝒱 : Y.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) :
147	    𝒱.pullback f ≤ 𝒰.pullback f :=
148	  fun x ↦ ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE (h (f.base x)))).le
149	
150	end PointedCover
151	
152	/-! ## Unit cocycles on a pointed cover and their restriction -/
153	
154	/-- The unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles of `X` on a pointed cover. -/
155	abbrev unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type u :=
156	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
157	
158	/-- The unit-valued Čech `H¹` of `X` on a pointed cover. -/
159	abbrev unitsH1 (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type u :=
160	  PresheafOfGroups.H1 (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
161	
162	/-- Restriction of unit Čech classes along a refinement of pointed covers, as a group
163	homomorphism. -/
164	def unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) : X.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 𝒱 :=
165	  H1.resHom fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)
166	
167	/-- Restriction along refinements of pointed covers is strictly functorial. -/
168	@[simp]
169	lemma unitsRes_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h₁ : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱)
170	    (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : unitsRes h₂ (unitsRes h₁ a) = unitsRes (h₂.trans h₁) a :=
171	  H1.res_res _ _ a
172	
173	@[simp]
174	lemma unitsRes_rfl {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {h : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
175	    unitsRes h a = a :=
176	  H1.res_id a
177	/-- If `U` is contained in the preimages of two opens, it is contained in the preimage
178	of their intersection. -/
179	lemma Hom.le_preimage_inf (f : X.Hom Y) {U : X.Opens} {V₁ V₂ : Y.Opens}
180	    (h₁ : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V₁) (h₂ : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V₂) : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (V₁ ⊓ V₂) :=
181	  fun _ hx ↦ ⟨h₁ hx, h₂ hx⟩
182	
183	/-- The pair value `γ.evInf i j` of a unit Čech cocycle, retyped as a unit section in
184	`Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)ˣ` (definitionally equal). Statements phrased through
185	`unitsEvInf` are honestly `Γ`-typed, so `rw`/`simp` work on them; goals arising from the
186	`OneCochain` field types are closed against them by `exact` (definitional bridging). -/
187	def unitsEvInf {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : X) :
188	    Γ(X, 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)ˣ :=
189	  γ.evInf i j
190	
191	/-- Restriction of a unit section along `W ≤ U`, as a group homomorphism between the
192	honest `Γ`-typed unit groups (definitionally the units-presheaf restriction map). -/
193	abbrev unitsRestrict (X : Scheme.{u}) {U W : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U) :
194	    Γ(X, U)ˣ →* Γ(X, W)ˣ :=
195	  Units.map (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
196	
197	@[simp]
198	lemma one_unitsEvInf {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (i j : X) :
199	    unitsEvInf (1 : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) i j = 1 :=
200	  rfl
201	
202	@[simp]
203	lemma mul_unitsEvInf {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (γ₁ γ₂ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j : X) :
204	    unitsEvInf (γ₁ * γ₂) i j = unitsEvInf γ₁ i j * unitsEvInf γ₂ i j :=
205	  rfl
206	
207	/-- The cocycle identity for the pair values, in unit-section language. -/
208	lemma unitsEvInf_trans {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j k : X) :
209	    X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
210	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)
211	        (unitsEvInf γ i j)
212	      * X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right :
213	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)
214	          (unitsEvInf γ j k)
215	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left :
216	          𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k ≤ 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)
217	          (unitsEvInf γ i k) :=
218	  γ.evInf_trans i j k
219	
220	/-- Restriction along a refinement, at the level of pair values. -/
221	lemma res_unitsEvInf {𝒲 𝒰 : X.PointedCover} (hle : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (γ : X.unitsCocycle 𝒰)
222	    (i j : X) :
223	    unitsEvInf (γ.res fun k ↦ homOfLE (hle k)) i j
224	      = X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_inf (hle i) (hle j)) (unitsEvInf γ i j) :=
225	  γ.res_evInf _ i j
226	namespace Hom

228	variable (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 𝒲 : Y.PointedCover}

230	/-- Pullback of the cocycle identity: the pair values of a unit cocycle on `Y`, pulled
231	back through `f : X ⟶ Y` to a common open `T`, still satisfy the cocycle identity. -/
232	private lemma pullback_pair_trans (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 : Y.PointedCover}
233	    (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (i j k : Y) {T : X.Opens}
234	    (e₁ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j)) (e₂ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k))
235	    (e₃ : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k)) :
236	    f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j) T e₁ (unitsEvInf γ i j)
237	      * f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T e₂ (unitsEvInf γ j k)
238	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T e₃ (unitsEvInf γ i k) := by
239	  have E : T ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) :=
240	    fun t ht ↦ ⟨e₁ ht, (e₂ ht).2⟩
241	  have ht := congrArg (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ⊓ 𝒰.opens k) T E)
242	    (unitsEvInf_trans γ i j k)
243	  rw [map_mul, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE,
244	    Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at ht
245	  exact ht
246	
247	/-- The pullback of a unit 1-cocycle along a morphism of schemes, on the pulled-back
248	pointed cover. -/
249	def pullbackUnitsCocycle (f : X ⟶ Y) (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
250	    X.unitsCocycle (𝒰.pullback f) where
251	  ev x y _ a b :=
252	    f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) _
253	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
254	  ev_precomp x y _ _ φ a b :=
255	    f.unitsAppLE_map (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) φ.op
256	      (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
257	  ev_trans x y z _ a b c :=
258	    pullback_pair_trans f γ (f.base x) (f.base y) (f.base z)
259	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (f.le_preimage_inf b.le c.le)
260	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le c.le)
261	
262	@[simp]
263	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_ev (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (x y : X) {T : X.Opens}
264	    (a : T ⟶ (𝒰.pullback f).opens x) (b : T ⟶ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y) :
265	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).ev x y a b
266	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
267	          (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le) (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y)) :=
268	  rfl
269	
270	@[simp]
271	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (x y : X) :
272	    unitsEvInf (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ) x y
273	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y))
274	          ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x ⊓ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y)
275	          (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
276	          (unitsEvInf γ (f.base x) (f.base y)) :=
277	  rfl
278	
279	@[simp]
280	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_one :
281	    f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (1 : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) = 1 := by
282	  ext x y T a b
283	  exact map_one (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
284	    (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))
285	
286	@[simp]
287	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_mul (γ₁ γ₂ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
288	    f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (γ₁ * γ₂)
289	      = f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₁ * f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₂ := by
290	  ext x y T a b
291	  exact map_mul (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
292	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))
293	    (unitsEvInf γ₁ (f.base x) (f.base y)) (unitsEvInf γ₂ (f.base x) (f.base y))
294	
295	/-- Pullback of unit cocycles commutes with restriction along a refinement. -/
296	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_res (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
297	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).res (fun x ↦ homOfLE (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h x))
298	      = f.pullbackUnitsCocycle (γ.res (fun y ↦ homOfLE (h y))) := by
299	  ext x y T a b
300	  have h₁ := congrArg
301	    (f.unitsAppLE (𝒲.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒲.opens (f.base y)) T
302	      (f.le_preimage_inf a.le b.le))
303	    (res_unitsEvInf h γ (f.base x) (f.base y))
304	  rw [Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at h₁
305	  exact h₁.symm
306	
307	/-- Pullback of a single coboundary comparison along a morphism of schemes: the honest
308	`Γ`-typed computation behind `pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous`. -/
309	private lemma pullback_coboundary (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 : Y.PointedCover}
310	    (γ₁ γ₂ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) (α : ∀ i : Y, Γ(Y, 𝒰.opens i)ˣ)
311	    (hα : ∀ i j, Y.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens i) (α i)
312	          * unitsEvInf γ₁ i j
313	        = unitsEvInf γ₂ i j
314	          * Y.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right : 𝒰.opens i ⊓ 𝒰.opens j ≤ 𝒰.opens j) (α j))
315	    (x y : X) {T : X.Opens}
316	    (ha : T ≤ (𝒰.pullback f).opens x) (hb : T ≤ (𝒰.pullback f).opens y) :
317	    X.unitsRestrict ha
318	        (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x) le_rfl
319	          (α (f.base x)))
320	      * f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
321	          (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb) (unitsEvInf γ₁ (f.base x) (f.base y))
322	      = f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T
323	          (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb) (unitsEvInf γ₂ (f.base x) (f.base y))
324	        * X.unitsRestrict hb
325	            (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base y)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens y) le_rfl
326	              (α (f.base y))) := by
327	  have h' := congrArg
328	    (f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x) ⊓ 𝒰.opens (f.base y)) T (f.le_preimage_inf ha hb))
329	    (hα (f.base x) (f.base y))
330	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE, Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE] at h'
331	  rw [Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map, Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map]
332	  exact h'
333	
334	/-- Pullback of a cohomology relation along a morphism of schemes. -/
335	lemma pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous {γ₁ γ₂ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰}
336	    (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂) :
337	    (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₁).IsCohomologous (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ₂) := by
338	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
339	  exact ⟨fun x ↦ f.unitsAppLE (𝒰.opens (f.base x)) ((𝒰.pullback f).opens x) le_rfl
340	      (α (f.base x)),
341	    fun x y T a b ↦ pullback_coboundary f γ₁ γ₂ α
342	      (fun i j ↦ hα i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)) x y a.le b.le⟩
343	
344	/-- The pullback of unit Čech `H¹` classes along a morphism of schemes. -/
345	def pullbackUnitsH1 (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) :
346	    Y.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 (𝒰.pullback f) where
347	  toFun := Quot.map f.pullbackUnitsCocycle
348	    (fun _ _ h ↦ f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_isCohomologous h)
349	  map_one' := congrArg OneCocycle.class f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_one
350	  map_mul' a b := by
351	    induction a using Quot.ind with | _ γ₁ =>
352	    induction b using Quot.ind with | _ γ₂ =>
353	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_mul γ₁ γ₂)
354	
355	@[simp]
356	lemma pullbackUnitsH1_class (γ : Y.unitsCocycle 𝒰) :
357	    f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 γ.class = (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle γ).class :=
358	  rfl
359	
360	/-- Pullback of unit `H¹` classes commutes with restriction along a refinement. -/
361	lemma unitsRes_pullbackUnitsH1 (h : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (a : Y.unitsH1 𝒰) :
362	    unitsRes (PointedCover.pullback_mono f h) (f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒰 a)
363	      = f.pullbackUnitsH1 𝒲 (unitsRes h a) := by
364	  induction a using Quot.ind with
365	  | _ γ => exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle_res h γ)

11	/-!
12	# Čech 1-cocycles: restriction, poset pair data, and commutative group structure
13	
14	This file extends Mathlib's fixed-family nonabelian Čech layer
15	(`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`, `H1`) with the three pieces of
16	infrastructure needed for a Čech-style Picard group (all stated generically; this file
17	is a Mathlib-PR candidate and contains no algebraic geometry):
18	
19	1. **Restriction along an indexwise refinement.** For families `U V : I → C` and maps
20	   `f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i`, cochains/cocycles/`H1`-classes restrict along `f`, strictly
21	   functorially (`res_res` holds on the nose at the cochain level).
22	2. **The poset bridge.** Over a poset with binary infima, a 1-cochain is determined by
23	   its values `evInf i j` at the infima `U i ⊓ U j` (`ev_eq_evInf`), and a 1-cocycle can
24	   be built from classical pair data satisfying the cocycle condition at triple infima
25	   (`OneCocycle.ofPairs`). Consumers never need to touch `ev` directly.
26	3. **Commutative group structure.** When the presheaf takes values in `CommGrpCat`,
27	   1-cocycles form a commutative group under pointwise multiplication (the cocycle
28	   condition for products needs commutativity) and this descends to `H1`; restriction
29	   is then a group homomorphism (`H1.resHom`).
30	
31	## Main declarations
32	
33	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.res`, `OneCocycle.res`, `H1.res`:
34	  restriction along an indexwise refinement, with `res_res` and `res_id`.
35	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCochain.evInf`, `ev_eq_evInf`: over a poset with
36	  binary infima, evaluation of a cochain at `U i ⊓ U j` determines it.
37	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs`: the classical construction of a
38	  cocycle from pair data `g i j` on binary infima with the triple-infimum condition.
39	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.isCohomologous_iff_evInf`: the coboundary
40	  relation in classical pair form.
41	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le`: if the members of the
42	  family are mutually comparable (e.g. all equal to a top element), `H1` is trivial.
43	* `CommGroup (OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` and
44	  `CommGroup (H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)` for `G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
45	* `CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1.resHom`: restriction as a group homomorphism.
46	-/

67	def res (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : OneCochain G V where
68	  ev i j _ a b := γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j)

74	    (γ.res f).ev i j a b = γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) :=

131	    (γ.res f).ev i j a b = γ.ev i j (a ≫ f i) (b ≫ f j) :=

172	    H1.res g (H1.res f x) = H1.res (fun i ↦ g i ≫ f i) x := by
173	  induction x using Quot.ind with
174	  | _ γ => exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (γ.res_res f g)

187	/-! ## The poset bridge: pair data on binary infima -/
188	
189	section Poset
190	
191	variable {P : Type u} [SemilatticeInf P] {G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}} {U : I → P}
192	
193	private lemma map_map (G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) {a b c : P} (h₁ : a ≤ b) (h₂ : b ≤ c)
194	    (x : G.obj (op c)) :
195	    G.map (homOfLE h₁).op (G.map (homOfLE h₂).op x) = G.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op x := by
196	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
197	
198	namespace OneCochain
199	
200	/-- The value of a 1-cochain on the binary infimum `U i ⊓ U j`. Over a poset with binary
201	infima this determines the whole cochain, see `ev_eq_evInf`. -/
202	def evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) : G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)) :=
203	  γ.ev i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)
204	
205	/-- Over a poset, a 1-cochain is determined by its values on binary infima. -/
206	lemma ev_eq_evInf (γ : OneCochain G U) (i j : I) {T : P} (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
207	    γ.ev i j a b = G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (γ.evInf i j) := by
208	  have h := γ.ev_precomp i j (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le))
209	    (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)) (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j))
210	  rw [Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le) ≫ homOfLE inf_le_left) a,
211	    Subsingleton.elim (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le) ≫ homOfLE inf_le_right) b] at h
212	  exact h.symm
213	
214	/-- Restriction commutes with evaluation at binary infima. -/
215	lemma res_evInf {V : I → P} (γ : OneCochain G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (i j : I) :
216	    (γ.res f).evInf i j
217	      = G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf (f i).le (f j).le)).op (γ.evInf i j) :=
218	  γ.ev_eq_evInf i j (homOfLE inf_le_left ≫ f i) (homOfLE inf_le_right ≫ f j)
219	
220	end OneCochain
221	
222	namespace OneCocycle
223	
224	/-- The value of a 1-cocycle on the binary infimum `U i ⊓ U j`. -/
225	abbrev evInf (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j : I) : G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)) :=
226	  γ.toOneCochain.evInf i j
227	
228	/-- Restriction commutes with evaluation at binary infima. -/
229	lemma res_evInf {V : I → P} (γ : OneCocycle G U) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (i j : I) :
230	    (γ.res f).evInf i j
231	      = G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf (f i).le (f j).le)).op (γ.evInf i j) :=
232	  γ.toOneCochain.res_evInf f i j
233	
234	/-- The classical cocycle condition for the pair values of a 1-cocycle: on the triple
235	infimum, `g i j * g j k = g i k`. -/
236	lemma evInf_trans (γ : OneCocycle G U) (i j k : I) :
237	    G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (γ.evInf i j) *
238	        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
239	          (γ.evInf j k) =
240	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
241	        (γ.evInf i k) := by
242	  have h := γ.ev_trans i j k (T := U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k)
243	    (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_left)) (homOfLE (inf_le_left.trans inf_le_right))
244	    (homOfLE inf_le_right)
245	  simp only [γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf] at h
246	  exact h
247	
248	/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data: values
249	`g i j` on the binary infima satisfying the cocycle condition on triple infima. -/
250	def ofPairs (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j)))
251	    (hg : ∀ i j k,
252	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op (g i j) *
253	          G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U j ⊓ U k)).op
254	            (g j k) =
255	        G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ⊓ U k ≤ U i ⊓ U k)).op
256	          (g i k)) :
257	    OneCocycle G U where
258	  ev i j _ a b := G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (g i j)
259	  ev_precomp i j T T' φ a b := map_map G φ.le (le_inf a.le b.le) (g i j)
260	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
261	    rw [← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) inf_le_left (g i j),
262	      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_right) (g j k),
263	      ← map_map G (le_inf (le_inf a.le b.le) c.le) (inf_le_inf_right _ inf_le_left) (g i k),
264	      ← map_mul, hg i j k]
265	
266	@[simp]
267	lemma ofPairs_ev (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j))) (hg) (i j : I) {T : P}
268	    (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j) :
269	    (ofPairs g hg).ev i j a b = G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le)).op (g i j) :=
270	  rfl
271	
272	@[simp]
273	lemma ofPairs_evInf (g : ∀ i j, G.obj (op (U i ⊓ U j))) (hg) (i j : I) :
274	    (ofPairs g hg).evInf i j = g i j := by
275	  change G.map (homOfLE (le_inf (homOfLE inf_le_left).le (homOfLE inf_le_right).le)).op (g i j)
276	      = g i j
277	  have h : homOfLE (le_inf (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)).le
278	      (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j)).le) = 𝟙 (U i ⊓ U j) :=
279	    Subsingleton.elim _ _
280	  rw [h, op_id, G.map_id]
281	  rfl
282	
283	/-- Round trip: rebuilding a 1-cocycle from its pair values gives it back. -/
284	lemma evInf_ofPairs (γ : OneCocycle G U) :
285	    ofPairs (fun i j ↦ γ.evInf i j) (fun i j k ↦ γ.evInf_trans i j k) = γ := by
286	  ext1
287	  ext i j T a b
288	  exact (γ.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b).symm
289	
290	/-- The coboundary relation in classical pair form: two 1-cocycles over a poset with
291	binary infima are cohomologous iff there are sections `α i` on the `U i` conjugating the
292	pair values into each other. -/
293	lemma isCohomologous_iff_evInf (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle G U) :
294	    γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂ ↔ ∃ α : ZeroCochain G U, ∀ i j,
295	      G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)).op (α i) * γ₁.evInf i j =
296	        γ₂.evInf i j * G.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U j)).op (α j) := by
297	  constructor
298	  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
299	    exact ⟨α, fun i j ↦ hα i j (homOfLE inf_le_left) (homOfLE inf_le_right)⟩
300	  · rintro ⟨α, hα⟩
301	    refine ⟨α, fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩
302	    have h' := congrArg (G.map (homOfLE (le_inf a.le b.le : T ≤ U i ⊓ U j)).op ·) (hα i j)
303	    simp only [map_mul, map_map] at h'
304	    rw [γ₁.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b, γ₂.toOneCochain.ev_eq_evInf i j a b]
305	    exact h'
306	
307	end OneCocycle
308	
309	/-- If the members of the family are mutually comparable (e.g. the family is constant,
310	as for a cover of a one-point space), then `H1` is trivial: every 1-cocycle is a
311	coboundary via `α i := γ.evInf`-type data at a base index. -/
312	theorem H1.subsingleton_of_forall_le (G : Pᵒᵖ ⥤ GrpCat.{w}) (U : I → P)
313	    (h : ∀ i j, U i ≤ U j) : Subsingleton (H1 G U) := by
314	  have key : ∀ γ : OneCocycle G U, (1 : OneCocycle G U).IsCohomologous γ := by
315	    intro γ
316	    cases isEmpty_or_nonempty I with
317	    | inl hI => exact ⟨1, fun i ↦ isEmptyElim i⟩
318	    | inr hI =>
319	      obtain ⟨i₀⟩ := hI
320	      refine ⟨fun i ↦ γ.ev i i₀ (𝟙 (U i)) (homOfLE (h i i₀)), fun i j T a b ↦ ?_⟩
321	      dsimp only
322	      rw [OneCocycle.one_toOneCochain, OneCochain.one_ev, mul_one,
323	        OneCochain.ev_precomp, OneCochain.ev_precomp, Category.comp_id, Category.comp_id,
324	        γ.ev_trans i j i₀ a b (b ≫ homOfLE (h j i₀)),
325	        Subsingleton.elim (a ≫ homOfLE (h i i₀)) (b ≫ homOfLE (h j i₀))]
326	  refine ⟨fun x y ↦ ?_⟩
327	  induction x using Quot.ind with
328	  | _ γ =>
329	    induction y using Quot.ind with
330	    | _ δ =>
331	      exact Quot.sound ((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).trans
332	        ((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).symm (key γ)) (key δ))
333	
334	end Poset

342	private lemma val_mul_comm {X : Cᵒᵖ}
343	    (x y : ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X)) : x * y = y * x := by
344	  letI : CommGroup ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X) := (G.obj X).str
345	  exact mul_comm x y

347	private lemma val_mul_mul_mul_comm {X : Cᵒᵖ}
348	    (a b c d : ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X)) :
349	    a * b * (c * d) = a * c * (b * d) := by
350	  letI : CommGroup ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X) := (G.obj X).str
351	  exact mul_mul_mul_comm a b c d

355	/-- The product of two 1-cocycles valued in commutative groups (the cocycle condition
356	for the product cochain uses commutativity). -/
357	protected def mul (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
358	    OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U where
359	  toOneCochain := γ₁.toOneCochain * γ₂.toOneCochain
360	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
361	    simp only [OneCochain.mul_ev]
362	    rw [val_mul_mul_mul_comm, γ₁.ev_trans i j k a b c, γ₂.ev_trans i j k a b c]
363	
364	/-- The inverse of a 1-cocycle valued in commutative groups. -/
365	protected def inv (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
366	    OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U where
367	  toOneCochain := γ.toOneCochain⁻¹
368	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
369	    simp only [OneCochain.inv_ev]
370	    rw [← mul_inv_rev, val_mul_comm, γ.ev_trans i j k a b c]
371	
372	instance : CommGroup (OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) where
373	  mul := OneCocycle.mul
374	  one := 1
375	  inv := OneCocycle.inv
376	  mul_assoc a b c := toOneCochain_injective (mul_assoc _ _ _)
377	  one_mul a := toOneCochain_injective (one_mul _)
378	  mul_one a := toOneCochain_injective (mul_one _)
379	  inv_mul_cancel a := toOneCochain_injective (inv_mul_cancel _)
380	  mul_comm a b := toOneCochain_injective (by ext i j T x y; exact val_mul_comm _ _)

404	lemma OneCohomologyRelation.mul
405	    {γ₁ γ₂ δ₁ δ₂ : OneCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
406	    {α β : ZeroCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
407	    (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) (h' : OneCohomologyRelation δ₁ δ₂ β) :
408	    OneCohomologyRelation (γ₁ * δ₁) (γ₂ * δ₂) (α * β) := by
409	  intro i j T a b
410	  simp only [OneCochain.mul_ev, Cochain₀.mul_apply, map_mul]
411	  rw [val_mul_mul_mul_comm _ _ (γ₁.ev i j a b), h i j a b, h' i j a b,
412	    val_mul_mul_mul_comm (γ₂.ev i j a b)]
413	
414	lemma OneCohomologyRelation.inv {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
415	    {α : ZeroCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
416	    (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) :
417	    OneCohomologyRelation γ₁⁻¹ γ₂⁻¹ α⁻¹ := by
418	  intro i j T a b
419	  simp only [OneCochain.inv_ev, Cochain₀.inv_apply, map_inv]
420	  rw [← mul_inv_rev, ← mul_inv_rev,
421	    val_mul_comm (γ₁.ev i j a b) ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map a.op (α i)),
422	    h i j a b,
423	    val_mul_comm (γ₂.ev i j a b) ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map b.op (α j))]

9	/-!
10	# The units presheaf of a scheme
11	
12	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of unit groups of the structure
13	sheaf on the small Zariski site (the poset `X.Opens`), valued in `CommGrpCat`, together
14	with the element-level interface used by the Čech `H¹` layer of the Picard group:
15	
16	* restriction of a unit section along `V ≤ U` is `Units.map` of the ring-level restriction;
17	* pullback of a unit section along a morphism of schemes, packaged as
18	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE` (the unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE`), with the same
19	  composition/restriction calculus as `appLE`.
20	
21	## Main declarations
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf`: the units presheaf
24	  `X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units`, a functor
25	  `(X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsPresheaf_map_apply`: restriction of unit sections,
27	  element form.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, `V : Y.Opens`,
29	  `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map`, `Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE`,
31	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE`, `Scheme.id_unitsAppLE`: the calculus mirroring
32	  `appLE_map`, `map_appLE`, `appLE_comp_appLE` and `id_app` at the unit level.
33	-/
34	
35	set_option autoImplicit false
36	
37	universe u
38	
39	open CategoryTheory Opposite
40

42	
43	namespace Scheme

45	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}

47	/-- The units presheaf `𝒪_X^*` of a scheme `X`, on its small Zariski site: the composite
48	of the structure presheaf with the units functor, valued in commutative groups.
49	
50	This is `abbrev` (reducible): the Čech layer constantly mixes sections typed through
51	`unitsPresheaf.obj` with sections typed `Γ(X, U)ˣ`, and rewriting across that boundary
52	requires the two to agree at instance transparency. -/
53	abbrev unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
54	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
55	
56	lemma unitsPresheaf_obj (U : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) :
57	    X.unitsPresheaf.obj U = CommGrpCat.of Γ(X, unop U)ˣ :=
58	  rfl

61	    X.unitsPresheaf.map i = CommGrpCat.ofHom (Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom) :=
62	  rfl

65	through which cocycle computations reach the `Units` API. -/
66	@[simp]
67	lemma unitsPresheaf_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
68	    X.unitsPresheaf.map i u = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
69	  rfl

72	`CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle`), element form. -/
73	@[simp]
74	lemma unitsPresheaf_forget₂_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V) (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
75	    (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map i u
76	      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
77	  rfl

79	/-- Split form of `unitsPresheaf_forget₂_map_apply`: after `Functor.comp_map` has fired,
80	the restriction maps appear as `(forget₂ _ _).map (X.unitsPresheaf.map i)`. -/
81	@[simp]
82	lemma forget₂_map_unitsPresheaf_map_apply {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V)
83	    (u : Γ(X, unop U)ˣ) :
84	    (forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map (X.unitsPresheaf.map i) u
85	      = Units.map (X.presheaf.map i).hom u :=
86	  rfl

90	variable (f : X ⟶ Y) {V V' : Y.Opens} {U U' : X.Opens}
91	
92	/-- The action of a morphism of schemes on unit sections: for `V : Y.Opens` and
